<SUMMARY>
The United States and India are nearing completion of a trade pact, with US Ambassador Sergio Gor indicating only 1% of talks remain, alongside a $3.3 billion Intel and 3DGS investment for a substrate plant in India. Global AI chip demand is creating bottlenecks in high-bandwidth memory, with Taiwan and South Korea emerging as central to AI infrastructure supply chains, while China's ByteDance develops custom AI CPUs to reduce US reliance. In West Asia, the US Treasury seized $1 billion in cryptocurrencies from Iran, coinciding with reports of UAE, US, and Israel airstrikes on Iran, and ongoing US-Iran diplomatic discussions. Geopolitical competition intensified in Oceania, where the Quad announced plans to develop ports in Fiji to counter China's regional influence, and Congo implemented cobalt export restrictions, boosting prices.
</SUMMARY>
<EWS>
AI chip scarcity poses a significant threat to advanced technology initiatives, as evidenced by SpaceX admitting its orbital AI ambitions are limited by scarce GPUs and uncertain semiconductor partnerships. Uber exhausted its full-year 2026 artificial intelligence budget by April. Geopolitical tensions in West Asia remain high, with reports of UAE, US, and Israel airstrikes on Iran, and warnings that potential Iranian control over the Strait of Hormuz could threaten US security and global freedom of navigation. The Middle East war is straining energy supplies according to the IMF and World Bank. Domestically, America’s grid faces strain from AI data centers and early May heat waves, contributing to power uncertainty across regions like DC and Philadelphia.
</EWS>
<EXEC>
**Asia:**
Anthropic's offhand mention of "logic chips" has fueled speculation in Korean media regarding a Samsung Foundry tie-up. Taiwan's entire supply chain, including Foxconn, is becoming the backbone of AI infrastructure, powering a 2026 growth sprint amid a trillion-dollar AI spending wave. Taiyo Yuden in Japan observes "scary" levels of AI parts demand, risking supply chain stability. TikTok owner ByteDance in China is reportedly developing its own custom AI CPUs to reduce dependence on US chipmakers. Huawei is betting on speed over shrinking transistors to sidestep US chip sanctions. Samsung Electronics and LG Uplus signed a memorandum of understanding on May 27 to jointly develop Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC) technology, enabling mobile network base stations to double as environmental sensors for 6G.

**Africa:**
Congo’s cobalt export restrictions are boosting prices and spurring sustainable growth for the EGC. Zimbabwe secured $1 billion in value-added lithium investments from China.

**Europe:**
Mistral AI hosted a summit in Paris, outlining its strategy to become the European full-stack AI partner by focusing on open models and on-prem deployment. The EU seeks to boost Europe’s chip demand as part of a tech sovereignty bid and plans to incentivize governments to buy EU-made chips from startups. Europe is actively developing a post-fab semiconductor strategy that emphasizes chiplets and ecosystem integration, aligning with a Chips Act 2.0 scheduled for 2026.

**Americas:**
SpaceX admitted its orbital AI ambitions depend heavily on scarce GPUs and uncertain semiconductor partnerships concerning the TeraFab project. AI chip startup Groq is reportedly raising $650 million in internal funding to pivot from hardware to AI inference. The US Commerce Department reported the goods trade deficit narrowed to $82.4 billion in April from $85.3 billion in March, as exports surged. Scott Bessent, speaking at the Reagan Presidential Foundation, laid out President Trump's economic doctrine and warned of US manufacturing vulnerabilities, tying economic resilience to a digital asset strategy. GraniteShares filed for a Speed of Light AI ETF, targeting photonics and AI infrastructure. A US semiconductor foundry secured a $936,000 contract from Huhutech. AI data centers are reshaping America’s grid, contributing to power uncertainty during an early May heat wave from DC to Philadelphia. A "left-right coalition" is forming against AI data centers in the US. Olivia White and Tiago Devesa argue the United States will continue to need trusted trading partners in the economy of tomorrow. Rio Tinto Group's aluminum exports to the US have rebounded to levels seen before President Donald Trump’s tariff offensive.
</EXEC>
<LITHO>
**Europe:**
ASML, a Dutch firm, is considered a critical firm atop the semiconductor market. ASML shares are up 53% in 2026.
</LITHO>
<REE>
**Africa:**
Congo’s cobalt export restrictions are boosting prices and spurring sustainable growth for the EGC. Zimbabwe secured $1 billion in value-added lithium investments from China.

**Americas:**
Viridis is in advanced talks for a Brazil rare earths project, having recently inaugurated its rare earths center in Poços de Caldas.
</REE>
<GEO>
**Asia:**
The shift in China-US relations is recasting the Quad, with India emerging as a strategic cog and the Quad serving as a tool for the Indo-Pacific.

**Africa:**
Mutasim Ali highlights the moral imperative of Sudan, explaining why "all eyes" are not on the conflict there.

**Europe:**
The Bank of England governor warned that a ceasefire would create uncertainty, not rate cuts, emphasizing the complex interplay between geopolitical events and economic policy. Palantir, a US tech giant, secured a controversial £330 million contract from the UK National Health Service (NHS), granting it "unlimited access" to patient data.

**Oceania:**
The Quad alliance is looking to develop ports in Fiji as a counter to China's rise, potentially creating a new US-China flashpoint. Foreign Policy and Asia Times articles reinforce that the Quad has a vital role to play, even with President Trump.
</GEO>
<MILITARY>
**Americas:**
SpaceX admitted its orbital AI ambitions depend heavily on scarce GPUs and uncertain semiconductor partnerships surrounding the TeraFab project.

**Oceania:**
The Quad is looking to develop ports in Fiji, creating a new US-China flashpoint. Australia's Defence Chief engaged in a debate, clashing on maritime chaos and the Hormuz crisis.
</MILITARY>
<CONCLUSION>
**Asia:**
Taiwan and South Korea are solidifying their roles as critical hubs for AI chip production and supply chain infrastructure, even as China's ByteDance seeks to reduce reliance on US chipmakers. Japan also faces "scary" AI parts demand.

**Africa:**
African nations like Congo and Zimbabwe are strategically leveraging their critical mineral resources, specifically cobalt and lithium, to attract investment and influence global market prices through export controls.

**Europe:**
Europe is actively pursuing semiconductor sovereignty and AI leadership through strategic initiatives such as Mistral AI's expansion and EU policies designed to boost local chip demand and manufacturing.

**Americas:**
The United States faces challenges in securing sufficient AI chips for ambitious projects like orbital AI, while domestic economic policy under President Trump emphasizes manufacturing resilience and digital assets. Concerns are rising regarding the energy demands and grid strain caused by AI data centers.

**Oceania:**
The Quad alliance is actively countering China's influence in the Indo-Pacific by investing in critical infrastructure projects, such as port development in Fiji, underscoring persistent geopolitical competition in the region.
</CONCLUSION>
<INDIA>
Intel and 3DGS, in collaboration with the Odisha government, signed a Memorandum of Understanding to establish a $3.3 billion substrate plant in Bhubaneswar-Khurda. This initiative aims to bolster India's semiconductor mission, reduce import reliance, and enhance global chip supply chain resilience. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor stated that an India-US trade pact may be weeks away, with only 1% of trade deal talks remaining. He characterized the India-US relationship as the defining partnership of the 21st century, driven by technology, strategic trust, and economic cooperation. A high-level US trade delegation is expected from June 1-4 to finalize the agreement. The Tamil Nadu government intensified its crackdown on illegal mining and quarrying, acting on complaints of mineral extraction beyond approved limits and environmental norm violations.
</INDIA>
<WEST_ASIA>
The United Nations blacklisted Israel and Russia for sexual violence in conflict; both countries refuted the allegations and accused the agency of bias. The EU expanded sanctions on Hamas and Islamic Jihad, imposing asset freezes and travel bans on 10 Hamas Politburo members over terror ties. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the US has "outright grabbed" approximately $1 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from Iran through seizures. Reports indicate the UAE carried out dozens of airstrikes on Iran alongside the US and Israel during the war. Amid US-Iran talks, a former senior US diplomat noted "fundamentally different ideas" cloud the negotiations, while optimism for a ceasefire deal is linked to gas prices sinking and oil being set for a 20% drop in May. The IMF, World Bank, and other organizations warned that the Middle East war is straining energy supplies. Analysts suggest that oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz might not return to levels seen before the Iran war. Concerns were raised that giving Iran control of the Strait of Hormuz would embolden Russia to seize the Arctic Northern Sea Route, threatening US security and global freedom of navigation. The Dow Jones edged higher, buoyed by optimism over US-Iran talks. The war in Iran has realigned Europe's energy future around America.
</WEST_ASIA>
<FINAL_CONCLUSION>
The coming weeks will be critical for US-India trade relations, with a significant $3.3 billion Intel/3DGS semiconductor investment poised to solidify India's role in the global chip supply chain. Simultaneously, geopolitical competition in the Indo-Pacific is underscored by Quad activities in Fiji, indicating increasing regional instability. West Asia remains a flashpoint, with ongoing US-Iran diplomatic efforts complicated by reports of UAE, US, and Israel airstrikes and financial sanctions, alongside wider warnings of energy supply strain due to regional conflict. The global race for AI chip supremacy and critical minerals is intensifying, with major investments and strategic actions by nations and corporations shaping future technological and economic landscapes.
</FINAL_CONCLUSION>
